messages:
tina (support): FYI customer escalation — multiple tenants seeing 502/504s hitting hosted inference (us-west-2) since ~10:04 PST. They provided a minimal repro and say it spikes when they fan out many small concurrent requests.

Example repro (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer SK_xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hello"}'
```

Trace IDs from customer: trace-09a7f3b2, trace-09a7f3c5

eli (eng-sre): Acknowledged. Do we have upstream auth-proxy traces or envoy logs? Is this correlated with any deploys?

tina (support): No deploys at that window per the customer. I pulled edge logs and saw repeated upstream 503 from auth-proxy right before envoy returned 502s to client. Snippet: 
```
[10:04:12] auth-proxy ERROR: timed out validating token, queue_len=180
[10:04:12] envoy WARN: upstream reset: authority=auth-proxy downstream_reset=connection_failure
[10:04:13] envoy ERROR: response_code: 502, upstream_code: 503
```

dana (runtime-oncall): Looking at metrics now — envoys in that AZ show active connections spiked from 300->1200 at 10:04. h2 concurrent_streams hit configured limit and listener queue depth increased. Looks like HTTP/2 stream saturation + upstream backpressure.

jamal (infra): Oncall checked host-level: auth-proxy pod restarted a few times around 10:05 with oom_kill in kern logs. Also noticed ingress keepalive pool exhaustion on the nginx side. Could be thundering herd on token validation cache.

tina (support): Customer says their pattern is fanout of small requests (webhooks -> inference per event). They can't throttle right now. Need quick mitigation so their app doesn't error. Any temporary fixes we can push at the edge?

eli (eng-sre): Short term plan: 1) adjust envoy config to lower per-connection concurrent streams and increase connection pool so requests are spread across more upstream conns, 2) enable tenant-level soft rate-limit (429) to give upstream backpressure, 3) temporarily disable disk-backed auth-cache to avoid heavy eviction thrash. I'll push a config change to canary.

deploy-bot: deploy config edge/us-west-2 change (reduce max_concurrent_streams -> 100, upstream_pool_size -> 50) started at 1766010100. Canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%

dana (runtime-oncall): Also reduced auth-proxy worker_threads from 16->8 and turned off local persistent cache to test. Monitoring heap and restart count.

tina (support): Customer reports partial improvement ~5m after canary: 502s largely stopped, occasional 504s still happening under peak. They confirmed they can implement client-side retries but asked for a long-term fix since their workload is high QPS with many small payloads.

eli (eng-sre): Long-term follow-ups: - repro in staging with h2 client opening many concurrent streams (will script), - heap/profile auth-proxy to find leak or pathological eviction, - add circuit-breaker + fallback token validation path that reads cached TTLed tokens, - add jitter to billing/job tasks that touch same cache keys.

jamal (infra): Noted correlation with scheduled billing job spike at 10:03 that also hits auth cache heavily. Recommend adding per-key locks and randomized delays on that job. I'll open infra ticket.

tina (support): I've provided customer with recommended client-side headers (Retry-After, exponential backoff) and a status update. Escalation ticket created and shared with customer.

eli (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem if this recurs. Assigning follow-up tasks: repro + profiler (ENG-SRE-3421), auth-proxy circuit-breaker design (RUNTIME-1284), infra job hardening (INFRA-2090).

tina (support): Thanks, team. I'll mark this as high-priority and loop in account on next steps. :thumbsup:
